## Heavy Water (D2O) Thermophysical Properties

Heavy water (deuterium oxide, D2O) is a form of water containing a higher proportion of deuterium (heavy hydrogen, ²H) rather than common hydrogen (¹H). This calculator provides key thermodynamic properties of heavy water.

### Key Properties Reference

| Property | Value | Unit |
|----------|-------|------|
| Boiling Temperature | 101.40 | °C |
| Melting Temperature | 3.81 | °C |
| Critical Temperature | 370.697 | °C |
| Critical Pressure | 21.671 | MPa |
| Critical Density | 0.356 | g/cm³ |
| Maximum Density | 1105.9 | kg/m³ |
| Molar Mass | 20.02751 | g/mol |
| Specific Heat (Cp at 20°C) | 4.219 | kJ/kgK |
| Latent Heat of Fusion | 306.2 | kJ/kg |
| Latent Heat of Evaporation | 2073.20 | kJ/kg |
| Surface Tension (at 25°C) | 71.87 | dyn/cm |
| Viscosity (at 20°C) | 1.251 | cP |
| pD (at 25°C) | 7.43 | - |
